{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "ajtowns",
      "stance": "neutral",
      "note": "argued that the budget wrapper's lifetime is explicit and scoped"
    },
    {
      "login": "maflcko",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "reviewed, questioned complexity of later commits, gave lgtm, and warned against LLM usage"
    },
    {
      "login": "Yudis-bit",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "previously warned of block download stalling; accepted deferring peer disconnect handling and ACKed"
    },
    {
      "login": "l0rinc",
      "stance": "support",
      "note": "ACKed the simplified approach, benchmarked decoding, proposed suggestions on bounds, tests, release notes, and shared parsing logic, and pushed back on tight deserialization limits"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "rc:4607370928",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Consider the wrapper approach where the budget lifetime is explicitly scoped to the wrapper or ParamsStream rather than using mutable state on streams.",
      "quote": "the lifetime of the budget there is just the wrapper, which seems fairly explicit to me?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author adopted wrapper approach with non-overridable parameter feature",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4621169370"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4621169370",
      "status_by_quote": "I've switched to your approach, but added a feature for parameters to declare they cannot be overridden"
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5977344049",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "usefulness",
      "text": "Explain whether the complexity and minimal CPU cost of the last few commits is worth it given other memory-eating places in Bitcoin Core.",
      "quote": "Are they really worth the complexity (and minimal cpu cost) when there are other places in Bitcoin Core that can eat memory (including in p2p). Are we going to address all of them?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author agreed the performance gains did not justify the complexity and dropped all but the first two commits",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:7021692240",
        "r:6006636619"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "r:6006636619",
      "status_by_quote": "I have dropped all but the first two commits; I think it's fair that the performance gains don't justify the complexity "
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4629170452",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Oversized blocks failing deserialization are not disconnected, so the block request stays in mapBlocksInFlight until the 10-minute download timeout expires, potentially stalling block download.",
      "quote": "Since the peer isn't disconnected, the hash stays in mapBlocksInFlight until the 10-minute download timeout expires.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "accepted leaving peer disconnect handling to a follow-up",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4629650852"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "c:7073149070",
      "status_by_quote": "Makes sense to keep just these two commits and leave peer disconnect handling for undeserializable messages to a follow-"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4697794157",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Keep block validation reasons covered through submitblock in feature_block.py now that P2P deserialization rejects them earlier",
      "quote": "These blocks used to exercise `bad-txns-vin-empty` and `bad-txns-vout-empty`. Now that P2P deserialization stops earlier, sending the same blocks through `submitblock` would keep both checks covered.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author implemented tests using submitblock",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4721068679"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4721068679",
      "status_by_quote": "Done."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4697799226",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Add a test checking that outputs survive a TX_NO_WITNESS round trip for zero-input funding templates",
      "quote": "A funding template can have outputs before the wallet picks any inputs. I’d check that those outputs survive a `TX_NO_WITNESS` round trip here.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added test",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4721074888"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4721074888",
      "status_by_quote": "Done."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4697812447",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "Add a release note documenting the new input and output count limits for RPC and kernel callers",
      "quote": "This also changes what RPC and kernel callers can inspect. A short release note with the two counts would help explain why a transaction that used to decode now fails.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author added release note for RPC callers",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4721089197"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4721089197",
      "status_by_quote": "I've added a short release note about the RPCs."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4697816420",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Check flags when reading zero-input transactions so incomplete output data produces an end-of-data error rather than superfluous witness record",
      "quote": "Getting `Superfluous witness record` when the output data is incomplete could be confusing for the user, we could also check `flags` here...",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author implemented the check",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4721112715"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4721112715",
      "status_by_quote": "Done."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4697823966",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "Share the upper bounds on block input and output counts between UnserializeTransaction and AccessByTxid",
      "quote": "`AccessByTxid` already calculates the same output limit. If we move the bounds here, it can reuse `MAX_OUTPUTS_PER_BLOCK`.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author shared the bounds",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4721114336"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4721114336",
      "status_by_quote": "Done."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4698378736",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Leave room above consensus limits so transactions slightly above the limit receive validation errors rather than decode failures",
      "quote": "I’d leave some room above the consensus limits - given this is meant to avoid extremes. For the one extra input in this test I’d still expect `bad-txns-oversize` from validation.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "contested",
      "status_note": "l0rinc pushed back that tight bounds risk rejecting consensus-valid values",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4721168486",
        "rc:4721389761"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4723320275",
      "status_by_quote": "Isn't the tight version more fragile, since we have to make absolutely sure that we don't accidentally reject consensus valid values - instead of making it so wide that only obviously wrong values are rejected early?"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4698381956",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Whether it makes sense to extract common transaction parsing logic between UnserializeTransaction and PR 36548",
      "quote": "Would it make sense to extract the common part here so we only have one place to update these rules?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "accepted",
      "status_note": "l0rinc accepted resolving after removing the lambda in PR 36548",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4721290405"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4723303040",
      "status_by_quote": "I removed the lambda in my latest push, let's see what the reviewers will think - can be resolved"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4698767540",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "Use expressions naming the serialized field widths rather than magic numbers for the minimum input and output weights",
      "quote": "I’d find these minimum weights easier to check if the expressions named the fields. `Txid::size() + sizeof(COutPoint::n)` shows where the 36 comes from, and `GetSizeOfCompactSize(0)` gives the empty s",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "answered",
      "status_note": "author declined, preferring magic numbers over mixing implementation sizeof with protocol/consensus sizes",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:4721304997"
      ],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "rc:4721304997",
      "status_by_quote": "I don't like using `sizeof` here."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "r:5954417316",
      "verdict": "",
      "reason": "no reason given: lgtm aaea7040575171c1d12887fa15e64bc201a3f67c~2",
      "substantive": false,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5977344049",
      "verdict": "",
      "reason": "lgtm 57a26d1a63091964dc7010f45b7d836e11561bda",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "c:7073149070",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "Makes sense to keep just these two commits and leave peer disconnect handling for undeserializable messages to a follow-up.",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "r:6061260754",
      "verdict": "ACK",
      "reason": "I’m glad you dropped the weight accounting and stream state - I was uneasy about touching that much serialization code for this, and the two remaining checks are much easier to review. I also prefer r",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "both",
      "areas": []
    }
  ],
  "notes": "sipa addressed and fixed several suggestions from l0rinc (submitblock tests, funding template tests, release notes, and shared bounds). sipa declined the sizeof suggestion and the suggestion to leave room above consensus limits, on which l0rinc pushed back.",
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "replying to l0rinc's pushback on tight bounds vs leaving room above consensus limits",
      "id": "rc:4723320275"
    }
  ]
}
